source.title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains in ℂ^N

accepted.question_text: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^N be a bounded convex domain whose boundary contains no non-trivial analytic discs. Must it be true that there is no example in which Ω is essentially visible but not visible? Equivalently, does there exist such a bounded convex domain that is essentially visible, in the sense that for every pair of distinct boundary points p and q there is a compact set K ⊂⊂ Ω met by some geodesic segment joining any sequences z_k → p and w_k → q, but not visible in the stronger sense that every such sequence of geodesic segments must eventually meet a fixed compact set? The paper also asks the same existence question under the additional assumption that Ω is smoothly bounded.

evidence.quote: Question 3.3. Does there exist a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ C^N with no non-trivial analytic discs in the boundary which is essentially visible but not visible? Does there exist a smoothly bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ C^N which is essentially visible but not visible?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^N be a bounded convex domain, and let {γ_k} be a sequence of non-visible geodesic segments, meaning that γ_k([0,1]) eventually avoids every compact subset of Ω while the endpoints satisfy γ_k(0) → p and γ_k(1) → q for two distinct boundary points p,q ∈ ∂Ω. Define the boundary cluster set Γ({γ_k}) = {x ∈ ∂Ω : there exist indices k_n and parameters t_{k_n} ∈ [0,1] such that γ_{k_n}(t_{k_n}) → x}. If p and q are two distinct points of Γ({γ_k}), must one of the following two alternatives always hold: either the open real segment {tp + (1−t)q : 0 < t < 1} lies in Ω, or the closed real segment {tp + (1−t)q : 0 ≤ t ≤ 1} lies in ∂Ω and the complex affine line through p and q, namely (ℂ(p−q)+q), does not meet Ω?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.5. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Let {γk} be a sequence of non-visible geodesic segments and let Γ({γk}) := {p ∈ ∂Ω : ∃{tkn } ⊂ [0, 1] : limn→∞ γkn(tkn) = p}. If p, q ∈ Γ({γk}) and p ̸= q then • either {tp + (1 − t)q, 0 < t < 1} ⊂ Ω, • or, {tp + (1 − t)q, 0 ≤ t ≤ 1} ⊂ ∂Ω and (C(p − q) + q) ∩ Ω = ∅.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^N be a bounded convex domain such that every complex geodesic φ: 𝔻 → Ω extends continuously to the closed unit disc, or equivalently continuously up to ∂𝔻. Is that extension property by itself sufficient to force Ω to be visible? Put contrapositively, can there exist a bounded convex domain that is not visible even though every complex geodesic extends continuously to the boundary of the source disc?

evidence.quote: Question 3.7. Does there exist a non-visible bounded convex domain Ω such that every complex geodesic φ : D → Ω extends continuously up to ∂D? In other words, is the continuous extension of all complex geodesics up to the boundary sufficient for visibility?

accepted.question_text: For a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ ℂ^N, call Ω complex visible if for every pair of distinct boundary points p,q ∈ ∂Ω there exists a compact set K ⊂⊂ Ω such that whenever z_k → p and w_k → q, every sequence of complex geodesics φ_k with z_k,w_k ∈ φ_k(𝔻) satisfies φ_k(𝔻) ∩ K ≠ ∅ for all sufficiently large k. Is this notion actually equivalent to ordinary visibility? In other words, is a bounded convex domain visible if and only if it is complex visible?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.9. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Then Ω is visible if and only if it is complex visible.

accepted.question_text: Can there exist a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ ℂ^N that is not visible, but for which every geodesic ray γ:[0,+∞)→Ω has a landing point in the Euclidean boundary, meaning that lim_{t→∞} γ(t) exists?

evidence.quote: Question 3.10. Does there exist a bounded convex domain Ω which is not visible and such that all geodesic rays land?

accepted.question_text: Fix z_0 ∈ Ω for a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ ℂ^N, and let G_{z_0} be the family of all geodesic segments and geodesic rays starting from z_0, parametrized by hyperbolic arc-length. Is visibility of Ω equivalent to uniform equicontinuity of this family G_{z_0} as maps from [0,+∞) with its Euclidean topology into ℂ^N with its Euclidean topology?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.11. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Then Ω is visible if and only if Gz0 is uniformly equicontinuous (as family of functions from [0, +∞) endowed with the Euclidean topology to C^N endowed with the Euclidean topology).

accepted.question_text: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^N be a bounded convex domain whose boundary contains no non-trivial analytic discs. For a sequence z_n → p ∈ ∂Ω and a base point z_0 ∈ Ω, define the sequential horosphere E_{z_0}({z_n},R) = {z ∈ Ω : limsup_{n→∞}[k_Ω(z,z_n) − k_Ω(z_0,z_n)] < (1/2) log R}. Is it true that Ω has the Denjoy–Wolff property exactly when the closure of every sequential horosphere meets the boundary ∂Ω in only one point?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.8. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Assume ∂Ω does not contain non-trivial analytic discs. Then Ω has the Denjoy-Wolff property if and only if the closure of any sequential horosphere touches ∂Ω at just one point.

accepted.question_text: For a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ ℂ^N, is visibility equivalent to the Denjoy–Wolff property for holomorphic self-maps without fixed points? That is, does Ω enjoy the Denjoy–Wolff property if and only if Ω is visible?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.9. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Then Ω is visible if and only if it enjoys the Denjoy-Wolff property.

accepted.question_text: Let N ≥ 1 and let F: 𝔻^N → 𝔻^N be a holomorphic self-map of the unit polydisc with no fixed point in 𝔻^N. Must there always exist a coordinate index j ∈ {1,…,N} and a boundary point σ ∈ ∂𝔻 such that, for every initial point z ∈ 𝔻^N, the j-th coordinate of the orbit converges to σ; that is, lim_{n→∞} π_j(F^{∘n}(z)) = σ for all z ∈ 𝔻^N?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. Let N ≥ 1 and let F : D^N → D^N be holomorphic and without fixed points. Then there exist j ∈ {1, . . . , N} and σ ∈ ∂D such that limn→∞ πj(F◦n(z)) = σ for all z ∈ D^N, where πj(z) = zj (the projection on the j-th component).

accepted.question_text: Let Ω = D_1 × ··· × D_ℓ, where each D_j ⊂ ℂ^{N_j} is a bounded convex domain and each factor D_j has the Denjoy–Wolff property. If F: Ω → Ω is holomorphic and has no fixed point in Ω, must there exist an index j_0 ∈ {1,…,ℓ} and a boundary point p_{j_0} ∈ ∂D_{j_0} such that for every z ∈ Ω the j_0-th coordinate projection of the orbit converges to p_{j_0}, meaning π_{j_0}(F^{∘m}(z)) → p_{j_0} as m → ∞?

evidence.quote: Question 5.5. Assume that Ω = D1 × . . . × Dℓ, where Dj is a bounded convex domain in C^Nj, j = 1, . . . , ℓ and N1 + . . . + Nℓ = N ≥ 2. Suppose Dj has the Denjoy-Wolff property for every j = 1, . . . , ℓ. Let F : Ω → Ω be holomorphic and such that F has no fixed points in Ω. Is it true that there exist j0 ∈ {1, . . . , ℓ} and pj0 ∈ ∂Dj0 such that {πj0(F◦m(z))} converges to pj0 for all z ∈ Ω as m → ∞?
